numbers: תתקע"ד דורות (974 generations -- a known aggadic/Talmudic tradition, cf. bChagigah 13b-14a, of the generations 'contemplated before creation')
symbols_metaphors: משל כרם (vineyard parable): a vine/planting uprooted and replanted across generations, an image for the transmigration or succession of souls/generations
calculations_procedures: 974 generations reckoning tied to '1000 generations minus 26' aggadic tradition (Torah given at generation 26 of the 1000 destined) -- classic rabbinic numerology, referenced but not spelled out arithmetically on this page.

observations: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL NOTE: this page's opening line ('שמיני מאי הוי יש לו הקב"ה צדיק אחד בעולמו והוא חביב לו מפני שמקיים עולמו ומגדלו ומשמרו') is near-identical to p33-b2's opening line. Two possibilities: (a) the Bahir text genuinely repeats/echoes this formula at a later point as a rhetorical refrain, or (b) this is a page-rendering/scan artifact (e.g. a duplicate page in the physical exemplar, or misordered leaves). This is flagged as an open contradiction/duplication question for editorial review -- NOT resolved by this scan, since resolving it would require comparing against a second, independent copy of the 1883 edition.

The '974 generations' motif is a well-known aggadic number (Chagigah 13b) about the generations God 'thought to create' before the 1000 generations were reduced to the 26 generations from Adam to Sinai -- worth flagging as a strong candidate cross-reference to rabbinic/Talmudic numerology even though it is not a Tanakh verse per se.
